questions.prompt: Walk through what happens, layer by layer, when a user clicks Run on a FlowPilot workflow until the run detail page shows the result.

keyPoints.text: The frontend calls the execute route for the workflow.
keyPoints.quote: Frontend calls `POST /api/workflows/[id]/execute`.

keyPoints.text: The route validates tenant and workflow and creates a pending run record.
keyPoints.quote: creates a `workflow_runs` record with `pending`

keyPoints.text: The route does not execute anything itself; it enqueues a job.
keyPoints.quote: Route enqueues a job in `workflowQueue`.

keyPoints.text: The worker hands the job to the executor, which checks concurrency and idempotency and loads ordered steps.
keyPoints.quote: Executor checks concurrency and idempotency, loads ordered steps, marks run `running`.

keyPoints.text: Each step resolves its input mapping from the run context before the runner executes.
keyPoints.quote: resolves input mapping from `RunContext`

keyPoints.text: Each step is logged and published as a live event, and retried with backoff if needed.
keyPoints.quote: publishes SSE event for live UI

keyPoints.text: At the end the run is marked completed or failed, its context stored, and exhausted failures dead-lettered.
keyPoints.quote: writes `event_log` and dead-letter if exhausted

questions.prompt: Explain the key design decisions in FlowPilot's architecture and the trade-off each one accepts.

keyPoints.text: Next.js App Router hosts both UI and API in one codebase, at the cost of coupling them.
keyPoints.quote: app and API are tightly coupled; scaling API independently is harder

keyPoints.text: Drizzle schema-as-code makes tables, indexes and constraints reviewable in Git.
keyPoints.quote: schema-as-code makes tables/indexes/constraints readable in Git

keyPoints.text: Orchestration lives in a separate engine so routes stay thin.
keyPoints.quote: API should be thin; orchestration logic belongs in reusable services

keyPoints.text: The separation adds abstraction that juniors must learn.
keyPoints.quote: more abstraction to learn for juniors

keyPoints.text: Long-running steps go through a queue so they do not block HTTP requests.
keyPoints.quote: long-running steps should not block HTTP requests

keyPoints.text: Every endpoint answers with the same success/data/error envelope so the frontend parses responses uniformly.
keyPoints.quote: frontend can parse all endpoint responses consistently

keyPoints.text: Zod validates inputs at the API edge to reject bad data early.
keyPoints.quote: reject bad input early at API edge

questions.prompt: How does the code running today differ from the intended production architecture, and what technical debt does the guide flag?

keyPoints.text: The queue and Redis are in-memory shims chosen for local build reliability.
keyPoints.quote: current implementation uses **in-memory queue/redis shim** for local build reliability

keyPoints.text: The intended production target is BullMQ with Redis.
keyPoints.quote: Intended production target from prompt is BullMQ + Redis.

keyPoints.text: Production is meant to run separate app and worker containers.
keyPoints.quote: App container + worker container.

keyPoints.text: PostgreSQL and Redis are meant to be managed services.
keyPoints.quote: PostgreSQL + Redis as managed services.

keyPoints.text: The in-memory Redis substitute cannot serve multiple instances.
keyPoints.quote: in-memory Redis substitute (not suitable for multi-instance production)

keyPoints.text: The in-memory queue abstraction has no durable persistence.
keyPoints.quote: in-memory queue abstraction (no durable persistence)

keyPoints.text: Tests are mostly placeholders.
keyPoints.quote: Tests are mostly placeholders
